Image 2 is her son's character sheet: use it only for the skin tone of his hands, his sleeves or shirt cuffs and his single gold wedding band. Image 3 shows the brochure: use it only for its size and cover. Extreme close-up. The photo shows her son's two hands (deep brown skin, lighter palms, a gold wedding band, the cuffs of his plaid button-down shirt) hold the glossy senior-living brochure, cover facing the camera, in the hallway stacked with plain moving boxes; it is a thin brochure of only a few pages; both hands grip it near the top, close together at the middle, thumbs side by side on the front cover just under the title, ready to tear it straight down the middle; the whole title "WRENFIELD · SENIOR LIVING" is readable above his thumbs; his face is out of the frame. The brochure is a glossy senior-living brochure whose cover photo shows smiling seniors at a communal dining table. Every moving box is plain brown cardboard, unprinted and unlabeled, with no brand marks. Every hand has five fingers in natural proportion and a natural grip; each person has exactly two arms and two hands; nothing floats.
